title: Slow to Anger and Fast to Forgive: Cooperation in an Uncertain World
central_claims: In noisy repeated prisoner’s dilemmas, cooperation is higher when cooperative equilibria exist.
Lenient and forgiving cooperative strategies attain higher payoffs under those conditions, with strategic heterogeneity.

sources.title: Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics: supplementary materials, Tables S1–S2
sources.finding: The selected cooperation contrast reproduced: N=128, p<.001, r=.33, versus original N=124 and r=.30. Table S2 identifies the benefit/cost 1.5 versus 2 contrast. Independent data collection was led by Camerer and Nave; the consortium also includes original coauthor Dreber.

sources.title: Fast to Forgive, Slow to Retaliate: Intuitive Responses in the Ultimatum Game Depend on the Degree of Unfairness
sources.finding: Ferguson and colleagues explicitly integrate the original uncertainty/forgiveness idea into a hypothesis about unfair offers, testing it in ultimatum games. Mildly unfair offers elicited more acceptance with shorter delays.

sources.title: Individual versus group choices of repeated game strategies: A strategy method approach
sources.finding: Cason and Mui use the original parameters and twenty strategies for direct choices by individuals and groups. They identify group differences in forgiveness and persistent poor-performing defection. Publisher abstract, introduction and section excerpts were read; institutional metadata confirms March 2019.

sources.title: Fudenberg et al. replication protocol
sources.finding: The protocol names Camerer and Nave, a Claremont sample, original software and predefined analysis. This is a plan, not the final results table.

search_gaps: Original reading was the complete publisher abstract, not full text.
Replication consortium includes an original coauthor; the local replication team and collected data are independent.
No comprehensive review, operational adoption or comparison against newer alternatives was established.
Read-access limits: publisher excerpts for Cason/Mui rather than its complete methods/results.
summary: The selected cooperation contrast replicated, and independent researchers substantively reused and extended the strategy framework. This does not establish every claim or real-world adoption.
